options: Losing rows of data during a merge
Information that would not be available at prediction time getting into training or evaluation
A database connection that fails
Storing data in more than one file
questions.explain: Leakage lets a model 'cheat', which produces inflated scores that do not hold up on genuinely new data.

questions.q: You predict churn and one feature is refund_issued, recorded when a customer cancels. This is an example of:
options: A good predictive feature to keep
Missing data
Target leakage
Class imbalance
questions.explain: The refund is a consequence of the outcome, so it would not be known at prediction time. It must be excluded.

questions.q: Which question best catches target leakage in a feature?
options: Is this feature numeric?
Will I actually know this value at the moment I need to make the prediction?
Does this feature have missing values?
Is this feature correlated with anything?
questions.explain: A feature that is only known after the outcome (or derived from it) cannot be used in a real prediction.

questions.q: In the noise-labels experiment, why did selecting features BEFORE splitting produce about 79% accuracy?
options: The model found a real pattern
Logistic regression works best on noise
The test rows' labels influenced which features were kept, leaking test information into training
The split was stratified
questions.explain: Choosing features with all rows lets the test labels shape the model. With random labels, the honest score is chance, about 51%.

questions.q: What is the correct order for preprocessing that learns from data, such as scaling or feature selection?
options: Fit on the training set only, then apply the fitted transform to validation and test sets
Fit on the full dataset, then split
Fit separately on each of train and test
Fit on the test set only
questions.explain: Split first, fit transformations on training data only, then apply them to the other sets.
